cards.title: Common mistakes (and how to fix them)
rule: **Double subject:** ✗ *My father he is a teacher.* → *My father is a teacher.*
**Two linking words for one idea:** ✗ *Although it rained, but we went out.* → use only one: *Although it rained, we went out.* / *It rained, but we went out.*
**Comparatives and superlatives:** ✗ *more better, most cleverest* → *better, cleverest*; ✗ *She is the most intelligent than…* → *more intelligent than* / *the most intelligent in…*.
**Word order:** subject + verb + object: ✗ *Our team the final won.* → *Our team won the final.*

examples.text: My father he is a teacher.
Although it was raining, but we went out.

cards.title: Notes
body: **Checklist before you hand in:** Is there a verb? Only one subject? One linking word per idea? -s with he/she/it?
Many mistakes come from translating Tigrinya word by word. Read your sentence aloud in English.
Compare with *-er / more … than*; use *the -est / the most* with *in / of*.

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct and free from double-subject mistakes?

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** In English, a clause must contain only a single subject referent per verb.
The noun phrase 'My elder brother' is the subject of 'is studying'.

cards.answer: My elder brother is studying civil engineering at university.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct and free from double-subject mistakes?

options.A: My elder brother he is studying civil engineering at university.
options.B: My elder brother is studying civil engineering at university.
options.C: My elder brother, he is studying civil engineering at university.
options.D: My elder brother him is studying civil engineering at university.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
In English, a clause must contain only a single subject referent per verb. The noun phrase 'My elder brother' is the subject of 'is studying'.

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Options A and C contain a redundant pronoun 'he' immediately following the noun subject. This is a classic double-subject error caused by Tigrinya verb conjugation habits. Option B correctly eliminates the redundant pronoun.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ወግዒ ሓደ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ሓደ ዋና ባእታ (Subject) ጥራይ እዩ ዝወስድ። 'My elder brother' (ሓወይ) ባዕሉ እኹል ዋና ባእታ ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ድሕሪኡ 'he' (ንሱ) ምጥቃም ድርብ ዋና ባእታ (Double Subject) ዝበሃል ዓቢ ጌጋ ይፈጥር። ስለዚ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option B እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Because the physics laboratory was locked yesterday afternoon, ________ we were unable to perform the experiment.

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** 'Because' is a subordinating conjunction at the beginning of the sentence to connect the clauses.
In English, only one conjunction can connect two clauses; adding a second is a double-conjunction error.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Because the physics laboratory was locked yesterday afternoon, ________ we were unable to perform the experiment.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
'Because' is a subordinating conjunction at the beginning of the sentence to connect the clauses. In English, only one conjunction can connect two clauses; adding a second is a double-conjunction error.

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Students often choose 'so' (Option A) because in Tigrinya, it is natural to pair cause with result (e.g., 'ስለ ዝሓመመ፡ ስለዚ...'). Option D is correct because no extra connector is allowed.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
ኣብ መጀመርታ እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ 'Because' (ምኽንያቱ/ስለ ዝ-) ዝብል መተሓሓዚ ስለ ዘሎ፡ ኣብቲ ካልኣይ ሓረግ 'so' (ስለዚ) ምጥቃም ዓቢ ናይ ድርብ መስተጻምር ጌጋ (double-conjunction error) ይፈጥር። ስለዚ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option D ([No connector] - ዋላ ሓደ ቃል ኣየድልይን) እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Which sentence is missing a linking verb (is/am/are/was/were)?

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** Every English sentence expressing a state of being requires a linking verb ('is', 'are', 'was', 'were') between the subject and the adjective complement.
**Step 2: Watch out for the trap.** In Option C, the linking verb 'is' is completely missing.

cards.answer: My brother very hardworking and always studies late.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which sentence is missing a linking verb (is/am/are/was/were)?

options.A: She is an exceptionally clever student in our class.
options.B: They are from the southern region of Eritrea.
options.C: My brother very hardworking and always studies late.
options.D: We were delighted to receive your invitation.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
Every English sentence expressing a state of being requires a linking verb ('is', 'are', 'was', 'were') between the subject and the adjective complement.

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
In Option C, the linking verb 'is' is completely missing. In Tigrinya, the linking verb can sometimes be omitted in speech, leading students to translate directly as 'My brother very hardworking...', which is incorrect. Option C is the target error.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ 'ምዃን' ዘመልክቱ ሓገዝቲ ግሶች (linking verbs - is, are) ወግዒ ክጸሓፉ ኣለዎም። ኣብ Option C 'My brother [is] very hardworking' ክኸውን ስለ ዝነበሮ፡ እቲ ግሲ ብምጥፋኡ ጌጋ ኣለዎ። ተማሃሮ ብስሕተት 'My brother very...' ኢሎም ክጽሕፉ ይረኣዩ እዮም።

questions.q: The program coordinator congratulated the candidates ________ achieving top scores in the national exam.
questions.label: 4. The program coordinator congratulated the candidates _______
why: Answer B: on
The verb 'congratulate' strictly requires the preposition 'on' followed by a noun or gerund: congratulate + someone + on + something.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

similar.q: Correct: Nobody know the answer.
Correct: She never says nothing.

questions.q: The administrative assistant provided us with many useful ________ regarding the registration process.
questions.label: 5. The administrative assistant provided us with many useful __
why: Answer B: pieces of advice
'Advice' is strictly uncountable and cannot be pluralized with an '-s' suffix. To express plurality, we must use partitive phrases like 'pieces of advice'.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

similar.q: Correct: The informations are useful.
Correct: He gave me an advice.
similar.a: He gave me some advice / a piece of advice.

questions.q: Identify the sentence that displays correct pronoun placement for a separable phrasal verb:
questions.label: 6. Identify the sentence that displays correct pronoun placemen

options.A: Please turn off the light before you leave.
options.B: Please turn the light off before you leave.
options.C: Please turn it off before you leave.
options.D: Please turn off it before you leave.

why: Answer D: Please turn off it before you leave.
'Turn off' is a transitive separable phrasal verb. Noun objects can go in the middle or at the end. Pronoun objects ('it') **must** go in the middle: Verb + Pronoun + Particle.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

similar.q: Correct: Please suggest me a book.
similar.a: Please suggest a book to me.

questions.label: 7. The chemistry instructor told the students ________ any of t
why: Answer B: not to touch
This is a reported negative command. Negative commands are reported using the structure: reporting verb + object + not to + V (base).

questions.q: Choose the sentence that displays correct English word order (S-V-O):
questions.label: 8. Choose the sentence that displays correct English word order

options.A: The doctor the patient examined yesterday afternoon.
options.B: The doctor examined the patient yesterday afternoon.
options.C: Yesterday afternoon the doctor the patient examined.
options.D: Examined the doctor the patient yesterday afternoon.

why: Answer B: The doctor examined the patient yesterday afternoon.
English requires a strict Subject-Verb-Object (S-V-O) pattern. The subject is 'The doctor', the verb is 'examined', and the direct object is 'the patient'.

questions.label: 9. When I was a young boy living in the village, I was extremel
why: Answer C: of
The adjective 'afraid' must strictly be paired with the preposition 'of' (afraid + of + noun).

options.B: We had a delicious lunch in the school dining room.

why: Answer B: We had a delicious lunch in the school dining room.
The verb 'dine' ends in a single silent 'e'. When adding the suffix '-ing', the 'e' is dropped to form 'dining' (/ˈdaɪnɪŋ/).

similar.q: Complete: He has worked here ____ five years.

options.A: She has been living here since 2015.
options.B: She has been living here for 2015.

why: Answer A: She has been living here since 2015.
"since 2015" (a starting point) requires a perfect tense.
Use the present perfect (continuous): has been living.
"for" is used with periods (for ten years), not points in time.

options.A: my family and I; We swam
options.B: my family and me; We swim
options.C: my family and I; We have swum

why: Answer A: my family and I; We swam
"my family and ___" is the subject, so use "I".
"Last year" is finished past time, so use the past simple: swam (and ate).
Only the first option fixes both errors.

questions.label: 20. True or false: "Everyone have finished their work" is correct.

similar.q: Correct: Somebody have taken my pen.
